subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which policy shape is approved for core?
rationale: The request changes the browser egress security boundary and public config surface, and current source shows no existing confirm or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a staged core policy
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before considering interactive confirmation UX.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to user-approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, and audit semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation starts.

options.title: Reject core expansion
options.body: Keep the current strict default plus hostname exceptions and document that broad private-network access remains an explicit trusted-environment opt-in.

recommendation.title: Design a staged core policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before considering interactive confirmation UX.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history across the browser SSRF guard, strict defaults, shared SSRF policy, and docs that this security-boundary choice would change.
